description: A mission permits read, write and pay; send is denied by the compiled rule mission_tools at the plan authority.
write is permitted only in files: a write to the shared drive is BLOCK write_in_files_only (history carries the read, so the order rule is satisfied).
A mission can add a wait: the boss, who pays freely under the permanent rules, waits for the owner under m1 (mission_pay_approval).
PLAN ORDER AS HISTORY: write before any read is BLOCK read_first (the compiled rule counts read in the harness-supplied history, < 1).
With a read in history the write proceeds under the permanent limit rule: LIMIT small_writes.
The order rule needs history: a write with none supplied is BLOCK required_facts (a harness must always supply it).
A mission that permits send does not loosen the law: external mail is still BLOCK no_external.

builtin.text: Every fact a decision needs must be supplied and valid; a missing or invalid fact is never permission.
The call's arguments are an object whose fields are exactly the tool's declared fields, each valid for its bound fact; anything else is refused, never run.
Only declared scopes are governed; a call in an undeclared scope is blocked.
Only declared roles may act; unknown roles are blocked.
A tool may be called only in the scopes it declares.
A participant may only call tools its role lists.
A tool the rulebook does not know is denied, or waits for approval, as the rulebook says (otherwise).
A delegate may call a tool only if every role in its delegation chain lists it; delegated authority never grows.

findings.message: `cap` (set by owner) is already covered by `plan:tools` (set by Mission plan m2), which says the same thing (deny) for Worker, Boss · pay · everywhere, when projected_spend > 500. `cap` adds nothing. For example: worker does pay in files with amount=0, projected_spend=501.

`pay_waits` (set by owner) is fully covered by the stricter `plan:tools` (set by Mission plan m2): `pay_waits` (set by owner) says wait for approval by owner; `plan:tools` (set by Mission plan m2) says deny. `pay_waits` can never change a decision. For example: worker does pay in files with amount=0, projected_spend=0.

`small_writes` (set by owner) is fully covered by the stricter `plan:tools` (set by Mission plan m2): `small_writes` (set by owner) says limit max_bytes 1000; `plan:tools` (set by Mission plan m2) says deny. `small_writes` can never change a decision. For example: worker does write in files with path="x".

description: A mission that permits pay does not loosen the owner's cap: 501 projected is still BLOCK cap.
The mission rulebook has its own fingerprint (every decision under it carries it): the base rulebook's fingerprint is not it.
evaluatePlan on a /1 plan: read then write in files satisfies read_first (the first step is in the history the second sees), must_write and one_pay; the write is LIMIT without a size.
A plan that writes before reading: the write step is BLOCK read_first.
AT_LEAST: a plan with no write breaks must_write (requires), cited at the last step.
AT_MOST: two payments break one_pay; each payment step also waits (pay_waits and mission_pay_approval), and the approval requests are collected.
A /1 step lands in the scope it names (no continuity check: a call does not carry the participant): the write to the shared drive is judged there and the mission denies it.
A mission rulebook whose mission record is malformed is invalid.
